newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper, aluminium stocks may fall - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper, aluminium stocks may fall - trade.

text.p: Copper stocks on the London Metal Exchange (LME) will probably fall again by between 2,000-5,000 tonnes, Singapore metal traders said on Friday.

In the general view of traders polled by Reuters, aluminium inventories are expected to show a decline of around 2,000-4,000 tonnes in the LME stocks report due out at 0900 GMT today, although one said he did not expect any change in aluminium stocks.
"The (copper) stocks won't go down a lot. The substantial drawdowns we've seen in copper should be coming to an end soon," a dealer in a Japanese metal trading firm said.

Copper stocks have dropped by more than 130,000 tonnes since the beginning of September and traders remain divided on whether the material is winding up among end-users or just being transferred from one LME warehouse to another.

Traders said between 20,000 to 40,000 tonnes of copper should begin showing up in the LME warehouse in Singapore shortly. Stocks here have dropped to around 1,450 tonnes, driving up premiums over LME cash metal in the city-state.

"The expectation is that the amount coming here will range between 20,000 and 40,000 tonnes. It should start arriving very soon. Some of the stuff is from China but a lot of it is material that also never made it there," one dealer said.

Another dealer with a Western metal trading firm said the picture is confusing, with traders in his own office predicting copper stocks may show either a rise of 5,000 tonnes or a drop of 5,000 tonnes.
"That just goes to show how confused everybody is," the dealer said.
Three month LME copper was priced in Singapore at around US$1,935/40 a tonne at 0215 GMT, up slightly from $1,930/35 in late trade in London on Thursday.
Aluminium was being quoted here at $1,430/35 a tonne at 0215 GMT compared with $1,429/31 during late trade in London.
